---
title: "Correction"
---

Remotely sensing imagery occasionally requires pre-processing, as sensors may pick up distortions that may affect surface reflectance imagery from the bottom of atmosphere. This section will focus on correction and enhancements. The following study area of Hong Kong will demonstrate a workflow of mosiacking Landsat 8-9 tiles and imagery enhancements processed through R.

## Summary

Two main sources of environmental attenuation is atmospheric scattering and topographic attenuation. As irradiance travels through the atmosphere and reflects back to sensors as radiance, atmospheric absorption and scattering introduces "adjacency effect" which captures radiance from neighboring pixels rather than the target. These distortions can creates haze and reduce contrast in imagery, presenting the need for atmospheric correction to obtain true apparent reflectance.

Beyond atmospheric correction, remotely sensing data may also require geometric, orthorectification, and radiometric corrections to account for any sensor distortions, terrain displacement, and calibration errors. The following discusses the 5 main types of corrections.

#### Types of Correction

+---------------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Correction                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                            | Benefits                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Limitations                                                                                                         | When to use?                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

| Geometric Correction                        | Correct positional distortions from off-nadir view angles, topography, wind, earth shape and rotation                                                                                  | Aligning with Ground Control Points (GCPs) allows high accuracy                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Time consuming; Computational complexity                                                                            | Compared with data or maps; Calculation of distances or area; Two images acquired at different dates to be compared pixel by pixel. ([Green and Clark, 2000](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261795733_Geometric_correction_of_satellite_and_airborne_imagery)) |
+---------------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Atmospheric Correction                      | Removes atmospheric effects;                                                                                                                                                           | Removes haze and adjacency effects                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |                                                                                                                     | Need to acquire biophysical parameters (e.g. temperature, NDVI); Using spectral signatures through time and space                                                                                                                                                        |
|                                             |                                                                                                                                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                             | Methods: Dark Object Subtraction (DOS); Psuedo-invariant Features (PIFs)                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
+---------------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Empirical Line Correction                   | Uses field spectrometer for measurements taken during satellite overpass                                                                                                               | Provide a simple surface reflectance calibration: available invariant-in-time calibration target measurement ([Karpouzli et.al, 2003](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/200459166_The_empiracle_line_method_for_the_atmospheric_correction_of_IKONOS_imagery)) | Requires physical field measurement to be done exactly timed with satellite overpasses; Hazards may present on site | To obtain accurate and precise surface refection                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
+---------------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Orthorectification (Topographic) Correction | Assign coordinates to an image (Georectification) and Orthorectification goes beyond in removing distortions (influences of topography), ensuring pixels are as if depicted from nadir | Allow accuracy for terrain areas through removing terrain displacements                                                                                                                                                                                               |                                                                                                                     | For areas with complex terrain                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|                                             |                                                                                                                                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|                                             |                                                                                                                                                                                        |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                     | (Note\* Should be used after atmospheric correction)                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
+---------------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Radiometric Calibration                     | Convert Digital Numbers (DN) to spectral radiance                                                                                                                                      |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |                                                                                                                     |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
+---------------------------------------------+----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

## Application 

## Study Area: Hong Kong

Two satellite tiles were selected from Landsat 8-9 OLI/TIRS C2 L2, Collection 2 and Level 2 is selected for surface reflection (provides surface temperature as well) where . In this case, two tiles were sufficient to cover the boundaries of Hong Kong. One Landsat 8 and one Landsat 9 tile has been downloaded with \<10% cloud cover between 19th to 20th of March 2025.

::: {layout-ncol="1"}
![Tiles Selection: draw an area of interest to search for tiles within the boundary for tiles and data preview in EarthExplorer (Obtained from: [USGS](https://earthexplorer.usgs.gov/))](images/w3_images/aoi_landsat89.png)
:::

### Mosaicking and Data Processing

Merging and joining data sets feathers the images together, which creates seamless mosaic imagery. Note that it is important that the tiles share a common CRS before mosaicking. Below shows the two tiles separately and linear stretched merged in RGB imagery.

::: {layout-ncol="1"}
![Tiles Selection (Obtained from: [USGS](https://earthexplorer.usgs.gov/))](images/w3_images/rgb_merge_comparison.png)
:::

The plot below compares spectral behaviours to capture different surface features. Each band operates at a different wavelength, with Bands 1–7 at 30m resolution and finer at 15m for Band 8. Vegetation shows high reflection in Band 5 NIR and Bands 6–7 SWIR respond to soil moisture and vegetation water content, which is helpful in distinguishing types of land uses ([Wang et.al., 2008](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233783774_Sensitivity_studies_of_the_moisture_effects_on_MODIS_SWIR_reflectance_and_vegetation_water_indices)). Theses spectral characteristics provided useful insights for understanding our study area before anaylsis. More about Landsat bands can be found in [USGS](https://www.usgs.gov/faqs/what-are-band-designations-landsat-satellites).

::: {layout-ncol="1"}
![Landsat 8-9 Spectral Bands](images/w3_images/landsat_bands_panel3.png)
:::

Next, clip Hong Kong boundaries to the imagery. Hong Kong Planning Districts Boundaries Data were obtained from [Esri China (Hong Kong)](https://opendata.esrichina.hk/maps/7b854e8c055d448a8385f4e693c828d1/explore?location=22.385925%2C114.110150%2C11) and transformed to a common CRS to ensure consistency with the satellite imagery, which is then used to clip the raster images. This enables further processing in enhancements, looking at certain features or spectral traits, texture and principal component analysis (PCA).

### Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI)

The NDVI index is used to highlight healthy vegetation, the following equation is applied:

$$
NDVI = \frac{NIR - Red}{NIR + Red}
$$

NDVI uses near-infrared (NIR) and red spectral bands to display vegetation which is not visible under visible bands. Healthy and green vegetation reflects stronger in NIR while simultaneously absorbs Red through photosynthesis, this has led NDVI to be an effective indicator for vegetation health. More other ratios can be found in [Index DataBase](https://www.indexdatabase.de/).

::: {#Scatterplot layout-ncol="2"}
![NDVI](images/w3_images/m1_ndvi.png)

![NDVI Vegetation Cover Only](images/w3_images/vegetation.png)
:::

### Texture

Texture captures the spatial relationships between neighbouring pixels, highlighting different land surfaces' distinct structural patterns (e.g. bumpy forests, smooth grass, jagged rocks). Band 4 Red is often used for texture analysis as urban surfaces and vegetation respond very differently to Red wavelengths. Vegetation absorbs red light for photosynthesis while concrete and buildings reflect it, creating strong contrast that makes land cover differences structurally distinguishable.

Grey-level-co-occurence matrix (GLCM) measures the relationship between neighboring pixel pairs at a certain distance. The following equation is used to convert the stored DN values to true surface reflectance value for highlighting structural contrast, dissimilarity, homogeneity, angular second moment, entropy, GLCM mean, variance and correlation with GLCM:

$$
$$\rho = (\text{pixel\_value} \cdot 0.0000275) - 0.2$$
$$

::: {layout-ncol="1"}
![Textures of Hong Kong](images/w3_images/glcm_all_metrics.png)
:::

### PCA

Principal Component Analysis (PCA) allows reduction of multi-spectral data into uncorrelated, smaller dimensions while retaining most of the imagery information. Computing a PCA summary shows that

```{r, echo=FALSE}
cat(readLines("correction/pca_summary.txt"), sep = "\n")
```

| Metric                 |    PC1 |    PC2 |     PC3 |     PC4 |
|------------------------|-------:|-------:|--------:|--------:|
| Standard deviation     | 2.8232 | 2.0581 | 1.19101 | 1.02581 |
| Proportion of Variance | 0.4981 | 0.2647 | 0.08866 | 0.06577 |
| Cumulative Proportion  | 0.4981 | 0.7629 | 0.85152 | 0.91729 |

97% of spectral variance can be identified in PC1, PC2, PC3, and PC4.

::: {layout-ncol="1"}
![PC1-4](images/w3_images/pca_1-4.png)
:::

## Reflection

Luckily, Level 2 data are analysis ready data (ARD), no manual correction processes needed.

Hong Kong is a very interesting study area, where it comprimises one of the world's most dense urban areas while having about three quarters of land covered in vegetation ([Gov.hk](https://www.hketoberlin.gov.hk/download/Green_HK.pdf), 2013).
